Park and Recreation Commission

  MINUTES – JUNE 2, 2022

A meeting of the Inglewood Park and Recreation Commission was convened on June 2, 2022, via
Zoom. Commissioner Denmon called the meeting to order at 6:02 p.m. followed by the flag salute.

Roll Call

Present
  Commissioner Lee Denmon, District One
  Commissioner Jacob Fragoso, District Two
  Commissioner Cynthia McLemore, District Three
  Commissioner Christopher Beck, District Four
  Sabrina Barnes, Parks, Recreation, and Community Services Director
  Geoffrey Okamoto, Transportation Supervisor
  Gilbert Gonzalez, Graffiti Abatement Supervisor
  Brian Sousa, Recreation Supervisor
  Stephanie Maldonado, Senior Management Assistant
Absent
  Commissioner Henry Brown, Commissioner at Large

Public Comments

  None

Approval of the Minutes

  Commissioner Fragoso made a motion to approve the minutes from April 7, 2022.
Commissioner McLemore seconded and the minutes were approved as follows:

  Ayes: Commissioners McLemore, Fragoso, and Demon
  Nays: None

Staff Reports

  Stephanie Maldonado presented a staff report recommending the Park and Recreation
Commission recommend the Mayor and Council Members adopt a resolution accepting a donation
in the amount of $58,030 from the American Heart Association for Greenfield fitness stations for
Edward Vincent Park and amending the Fiscal Year 2021-2022 Budget to reflect the aforementioned
funds.

  Commissioner Denmon stated I’m assuming that’s the little fitness station that sits in the
park. Director Barnes stated we will be adding a new fitness station through a donation from the
American Heart Association who is a partnering with the NFL to fund six (6) Greenfield fitness
stations with a goal of installation sometime in July.

  1
   Park and Recreation Commission

  MINUTES – JUNE 2, 2022

  Commissioner McLemore made a motion to approve the staff report and Commissioner
Denmon seconded. The motion was approved as follows:

  Ayes: Commissioners Fragoso, McLemore, and Denmon
  Nays: None

  Stephanie Maldonado presented a staff report recommending the Park and Recreation
Commission recommend the Mayor and Council Members approve payment of an invoice in the
amount of $11,970 for Sculpture Conservation Studio of Constantinople for repair and conservation
services for the Helen Lundeberg “The History of Transportation” mural.

  Commissioner Denmon asked has the work had been completed. Director Barnes stated
yes.

  Commissioner McLemore made a motion to approve the staff report and Commissioner
Fragoso seconded. The motion was approved as follows:

  Ayes: Commissioners McLemore, Fragoso and Denmon
  Nays: None

  Stephanie Maldonado presented a staff report recommending the Park and Recreation
Commission recommend the Mayor and Council Members take the following actions:
  a. Adopt a resolution amending the Fiscal Year 2021-2022 Annual Budget to
  cover expenditure for the Playground Floor Resurfacing Project for
  playgrounds at various City parks; and
  b. Approve an agreement with Robertson Industries Inc. in a total amount not
  to exceed $199,770 to replace and repair playground surfaces at various
  City parks. (General Fund)
  c. Authorize an additional not-to-exceed - City controlled and directed-
  contingency of eight thousand ($8,000) dollars. (General Fund)

  Commissioner Denmon asked if the work is going to be $199,770 and what is the additional
$8,000 being asked for out of the general fund. Director Barnes stated that's the contingency, a fund
for additional repairs if needed.

  Commissioner McLemore made a motion to approve the staff report and Commissioner
Fragoso seconded. The motion was approved as follows:

  Ayes: Commissioners McLemore, Fragoso and Denmon
  Nay: None

  2
   Park and Recreation Commission

  MINUTES – JUNE 2, 2022

Verbal Reports

  Gilbert Gonzalez gave a verbal report on behalf of the Parks Administration regarding the
following:
   The Graffiti Abatement staff has been busy in all City parks. Siminski Park was spruced up
  and/or repaired due to vandalism. Districts 3 and 4 have been heavily tagged in the Darby
  Dixon area alongside Crenshaw Boulevard and 104th Street and Century Boulevard just east
  of Yukon Avenue.

  Brian Sousa gave a verbal report on behalf of the Recreation Division regarding the
following:
   Summer Day Camp: begins June 21, 2021, and ends August 18, 2021, lasting a total of
  eight weeks. Summer Camp serves kids, ages 6-12. Kiddie Camp locations are at
  Lockhaven Community Center and Siminski Park for ages 3 to 5. Summer of Champions
  Camp locations for ages 6 to 12 is at Rogers and Darby Park. Capacity has been reached
  at 3 of the 4 campsites with availability at Lockhaven. Full robust scheduling includes field
  trips, pool days with transportation to Vincent Park, morning enrichment including STEM and
  academic activities; traditional recreation with sports, fitness, and play.
   Swimming Pool: The Edward Vincent, Jr. Park Swim Complex will open on Wednesday,
  June 22nd, and close on Monday, September 5th. This year's offerings will include General
  Swim, Family Swim Nights, Youth and Adult Swim Lessons, Parent and Me swim classes,
  and lap swim. Registration for all classes is required in advance and by pre-registration
  only! Registration will be taken on a first-come, first-serve basis and will remain open until
  all classes are filled. For additional information, please contact the Parks, Recreation, and
  Community Services Department at (310) 412-8750 or visit the department website.
   Family Paint Day: Family Paint Days are back this summer! Classes are designed to allow
  families (ages 5 and up) to spend carefree afternoons painting, laughing, and creating
  memories. Instructors provide step-by-step painting instructions and everyone produces the
  same piece of art. All materials are provided. The next class is Saturday, June 25 from
  11:00 a.m. – 12:30 p.m. at Darby Park. The cost is $15 per person. Pre-registration is
  required. Register online at www.parksrec.cityofinglewood.org.
   Self-Defense Classes: Learn the art of self-defense through basic techniques. Students are
  taught to recognize and avoid dangerous situations, as well as how to defend themselves.
  Students learn awareness, avoidance skills, and physical self-defense. Classes are free and
  open to youth ages 4 and up and are held on Saturdays from 10:00 a.m. – 11:30 a.m. at
  Center Park. Pre-registration is required. Register online at www.parksrec.cityofinglewood.org.

  Geoffrey Okamoto gave a verbal report on behalf of the Human Services Division regarding
the following:
   Senior Center Classes, Programs, and Activities: Since the partial opening of the Inglewood
  Senior Center, we have been able to add a few more activities such as ping-pong and bridge.
  Seniors are still expected to wear face coverings, have their temperatures checked, and

  3
   Park and Recreation Commission

  MINUTES – JUNE 2, 2022

  provide proof of full vaccination. These measures are required to enter and participate in
  activities. These measures will continue until further notice to continue to ensure our seniors
  are as safe as possible.
    Transportation: Our Senior and Disabled Paratransit continues to provide trips to critical
  appointments such as dialysis and doctors' appointments. Drivers, as well as passengers,
  continue to wear facemasks coverings. We have also been scheduling our drivers to
  transport our seniors and persons with disabilities to other next-day requested appointments.
  They are also if resources are available, may provide same-day requests as well.
    Nutrition: We are serving approximately 300 seniors per week and continue to provide LA
  Food Bank boxes monthly and fresh produce weekly. Our Nutrition staff including our Home
  Delivery Meals staff continue to be dedicated to serving and delivering our seniors their daily
  meals. Our dining room is currently closed because of COVID. We do not have a timetable
  to open our dining room where our seniors can come and congregate.
    CACFP Program (Meal Program): Our CACFP program (Meal Program) started on Monday,
  October 4, 2021, giving Grab and Go meals to youth 18 and under. We are operating at
  Darby Park, Rogers Park, and Crenshaw Library five days a week, Monday through Friday
  from 2:30 PM to 4:30 PM. We are providing about 70 meals a day on average at all three
  sites.
    Summer Food: Our Summer Food Program will start on June 13, 2022. We will be serving
  at seven different locations to youth 18 and under. The sites are Ashwood Park, Crenshaw
  Library, Darby Park, Siminiski Park, Lock heaven Community Center, Rogers Park, and
  Vincent Park. We will be providing breakfast, lunch, and snacks at different sites and the
  times will vary according to the sites.

Director’s Report

  Director Barnes gave a verbal update regarding the following Capital Improvement Projects
and Department Operations:
   On May 4, 2022, bids were received for the Darby Park restroom project, expectation of the
  winner vendor is to go before Council on a date closer to the end of the month. We anticipate
  construction starting by July 30, 2022, and a tentative completion date of March 2023.
   Construction is underway at Edward Vincent, Jr. Park's restroom. It’s' about 35% complete.
  On June 1, 2022, I participated in the Planning Commission meeting where the Planning
  Commission approved the construction plans allowing construction to move forward to the
  next phase with a projected completion date of November 2022.
   During the new fiscal year, plans are to return to Vincent Park to replace the restroom located
  closest to the Playhouse and the Dennis Menace playground relocating it to make it more
  accessible and centered. A schedule for the project should be available within the next
  month pending funding.
   Bids are currently out on the Vincent Park Arbor Project, replacing the arbors located in the
  picnic area. Bids are expected to be submitted by next month.

  4
   Park and Recreation Commission

  MINUTES – JUNE 2, 2022

    Bid specifications are being developed for the replacement of the Darby Park walking track
  in its entirety.
    Commitments from the American Heart Association are expected for fitness stations at
  Rogers Park. Based on approval, the location of the stations will be where the wading pool
  is located. There is no anticipation of restoring the pool.
  Plans are being pursued to plant out the water fountain at Circle Park. Approval by the State
  has been received. Due to vandalism during COVID, we will also renovate the exterior and
  put plants in the planter. We are currently in search of a landscaping architect to act as our
  consultant as well as provide plant pallet recommendations for all parks and center medians
  throughout the city. Conversations with the Dodgers Foundation continue for funding to
  renovate the ballfields at Vincent Park.

  Commissioner Denmon asked if the same material was being used to resurface the
playgrounds at Vincent Park. Director Barnes stated we are using pour and place again however the
current vendor will be adding an extra guard on top of the flooring to help with wear and tear. The
current flooring is about 10 to 12 years old. Two sites at Vincent Park will be replaced, others will
receive patching and coating

  Commissioner Denmon inquired about the wading pool near the playground at Vincent Park,
asking are there any plans to do anything about it. Director Barnes stated there are no immediate
plans to address the pool. Decomposed granite in the general playground area and the fence around
the pool reconfigured to the pool footprint.

  Lastly, Director Barnes stated we are currently on boarding staff to serve during the summer.
Staff will undergo extensive training including general service, CPR, mandated reporter, and more.

Public Comments

  None

Commissioner’s Comments

  Commissioner McLemore thanked staff. Commissioner Denmon echoed Commissioner
McLemore’s sentiments.

With no further business, the meeting was adjourned at 6:36 p.m.
